messages.subject: extract posterior samples of random effects SD
parts:
Hi,

first of all: many thanks for the great rstanarm package! 

There is one thing I couldn't figure out, though: as i tend to use my own summary functions on the posterior samples, i extracted the posterior with as.data.frame(). However, when running a multilevel model with stan_glmer, I am missing the group-level "errors" in the posterior, e.g. the standard deviation of the intercept random effects. Am I missing something? Thanks a lot!

CU, Martin.

On Friday, August 12, 2016 at 9:26:09 AM UTC-4, schmettow wrote:
There is one thing I couldn't figure out, though: as i tend to use my own summary functions on the posterior samples, i extracted the posterior with as.data.frame(). However, when running a multilevel model with stan_glmer, I am missing the group-level "errors" in the posterior, e.g. the standard deviation of the intercept random effects. Am I missing something? Thanks a lot!

The posterior mean is printed by the VarCorr() function, which is called by the print method. The draws of that standard deviation are not stored. You can pretty much recreate its posterior distribution by taking the standard deviation of that parameter across groups at each iteration. Something like

mat <- as.matrix(post)
b <- mat[,grepl("^b\\[")]
summary(apply(b, MARGIN = 1, sd))


Ben

messages.subject: Re: extract posterior samples of random effects SD

On Friday, August 12, 2016 at 9:36:54 AM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:

mat <- as.matrix(post)
b <- mat[,grepl("^b\\[")]
summary(apply(b, MARGIN = 1, sd))

The as.matrix method for stanreg objects also accepts an optional argument regex_pars, so you can do

b <- as.matrix(post, regex_pars = "^b\\[")
